lessons.title: One Pair
lessons.concept: Drawing a Line from Dot to Dot

play.shortDesc: Join two dots with one line
play.targetObjective: Join the two matching letters with one line.
stepByStep: Put your finger on a dot.
Slide to the next square: up, down, left or right.
Stop on the dot with the same letter.
play.kidTip: Lines go up, down, left or right. Never corner to corner.
play.audioPrompt: Put your finger on a dot and slide to the dot with the same letter.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The whole skill is the drag. Let them draw wobbly lines; any line that joins counts.

lessons.title: Two Pairs

play.targetObjective: Join two pairs without the lines crossing.
stepByStep: Join one pair.
Join the other pair without crossing the first line.
If a line is in the way, draw round it.
play.kidTip: Lines can never cross each other.
play.audioPrompt: Join both pairs. The lines must not cross.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Drawing over a line cuts it. That is not a mistake to correct; it is how they learn the rule.

lessons.title: Go Around

play.shortDesc: Bend round a dot in the way
play.targetObjective: Bend a line round a dot that is in its way.
stepByStep: Find the pair whose straight path is blocked.
Draw round the dot in the way.
Then join the other pairs.
play.kidTip: If a dot is in the way, go round it.
play.audioPrompt: Some dots are in the way. Bend your line round them.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The shortest line is not always possible. A detour is still a good line.

lessons.title: Fill Every Square

play.targetObjective: Join every pair and leave no square empty.
stepByStep: Join the pairs.
Look for empty squares.
Make a line longer so it runs through them.
play.kidTip: Now every square must be filled. Make a line take the long way round.
play.audioPrompt: Join every pair, and fill every square on the board.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The new rule changes the puzzle: a short line can now be wrong. Point at the empty squares, not at the line.

lessons.title: Practice: Joining

stepByStep: Join each pair.
Check for empty squares.
Fill them, then you are done.
play.kidTip: No hints here. Take your time.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Practice mixes the boards from lessons 2 to 4.

lessons.title: One Way Out

play.targetObjective: Start from a dot that has only one way to go.
stepByStep: Look at each dot.
Find one that can only go one way.
Draw that step first, then look again.
play.kidTip: A dot in a corner, or next to a wall of other dots, has only one way out.
play.audioPrompt: Find a dot with only one way out. Start there.

lessons.pedagogyTip: This is the core strategy: never guess while a forced move exists.

lessons.title: Hug the Edge

play.targetObjective: Use the edge of the board to route a line.
stepByStep: Look at the dots near the edge.
A line along the edge leaves the middle free.
Fill the middle last.
play.kidTip: Lines along the edge often have nowhere else to go.
play.audioPrompt: Some lines run along the edge of the board. Find them.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Edges and corners are where choices run out first, so they are where to look.

lessons.title: Don't Box It In
lessons.concept: Spotting a Move That Traps a Colour

play.targetObjective: Spot the move that would trap another colour.
stepByStep: Before you draw, look where the line will go.
Check every other colour can still reach its twin.
If a colour gets shut in, take the line back.
play.kidTip: The shortest line can shut another colour in. Look before you draw.
play.audioPrompt: Careful! A short line here can trap another colour. Check before you draw.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Each board has a move that heads straight for the twin and makes the board impossible. Undo is the tool here.

lessons.title: Five Pairs

play.targetObjective: Plan five lines on a bigger board.
stepByStep: Do the forced moves first.
Then the edges.
Then fill the middle.
play.kidTip: Forced moves first, then edges, then the middle.
play.audioPrompt: Five pairs on a bigger board. Start with the forced moves.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Everything so far, together. Encourage the order: forced, edge, middle.

lessons.title: Practice: Planning

stepByStep: Find the forced moves.
Use the edges.
Fill the middle last.
play.kidTip: No hints here. Take your time.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Practice mixes the boards from lessons 6 to 9.

lessons.title: Big Board

play.targetObjective: Solve a seven by seven board.
stepByStep: Scan the whole board first.
Do every forced move you can find.
Work inward from the edges.
play.kidTip: Big boards are many small puzzles. Solve one corner at a time.
play.audioPrompt: A big board with six pairs. Solve one corner at a time.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Bigger is not different, only longer. Praise steady progress, not speed.

lessons.title: Walls

play.targetObjective: Join and fill a board with walls on it.
stepByStep: Walls are not squares to fill.
Lines go round them.
Squares next to walls often have only one way out.
play.kidTip: Walls make forced moves. Look at the squares beside them.
play.audioPrompt: This board has walls. Lines go round them, and you fill every other square.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A wall removes choices, which usually makes the board easier to reason about, not harder.

lessons.title: Exact Steps
lessons.concept: Counting the Length of a Route

play.targetObjective: Join one pair in an exact number of steps.
stepByStep: Find the dot with a number on it.
Its line must take exactly that many steps.
Count the squares as you draw.
play.kidTip: The number on the dot is how many steps its line takes.
play.audioPrompt: One dot has a number. Its line must take exactly that many steps.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Without the number this board has more than one answer; the count is what makes it solvable. A step is one square moved.

lessons.title: Bridges

play.shortDesc: Two lines cross on a bridge
play.targetObjective: Use a bridge so two lines can cross.
stepByStep: Find the bridge square.
One line goes straight across it.
Another line goes straight down it.
play.kidTip: On the bridge, lines go straight over. Use it both ways.
play.audioPrompt: This board has a bridge. Two lines cross there, one across and one down.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The bridge is the one exception to never crossing. Both ways must be used for the board to be full.

lessons.title: On Your Own

play.targetObjective: Solve big boards with no hints.
stepByStep: Forced moves first.
Then the edges.
Then the middle.
play.kidTip: No hints on this one. You know how.
play.audioPrompt: Seven pairs, and no hints. You know how to do this.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Hints are off by design. It is a teaching lesson, so mistakes still count as learning.

lessons.title: Practice: Dot Connect

play.targetObjective: Solve five mixed boards without help.
stepByStep: Read the board: walls, bridges, numbers.
Forced moves first.
Fill every square.
play.kidTip: No hints here. Take your time.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Practice mixes big boards, walls, exact steps, bridges and seven-pair boards.
